# Release Notes

## 0.43.3 - 2026-10-21 (deployed)

Environment: production. Production run `39624076224` deployed SHA `581efb313ddfc40ea0fa529d545e8643b409ed27` on **2026-10-21** after exact-main validation `39622895854` and explicit Environment approval. PATCH: decode gzip-compressed Telegram JWKS and token JSON without relaxing signature, claim, state, PKCE or replay validation. The deployed runtime also includes the reviewed public `/app/login/` entry requiring Telegram identity confirmation; ordinary bot entry no longer needs internal signed-link issuance.

Deployment revision/readiness readback passed at `2026-10-21T15:21:57.069785+00:00`. Direct read-only production verification at `2026-10-21T15:28:49.268171+00:00` confirmed the exact active SHA and loaded four signing keys from the live Telegram provider using the deployed module. All eight containers were healthy and public root/PWA returned HTTP 200. Two real HTTP/gzip/RSA regressions and both isolated PostgreSQL/HTTPS/Chromium runs (35 Django regressions each, synthetic Telegram provider) passed. Independent implementation reviews found no blocking defect. No financial writes or payment-provider calls were made by production probes.

**ARTIFACT DEPLOYED; original phone journey NOT YET ACCEPTED.** Native Telegram -> external Chrome/Safari -> correct-user PWA and genuinely new/existing production user journeys remain unverified. Synthetic-provider acceptance and live JWKS retrieval are not real-user login evidence. The owner reported complete desktop login before deployment; the desktop/mobile discrepancy and the operational trigger of gzip responses remain unproven. Existing browser sessions can survive a failed repeat callback, but this is not a diagnosis of the owner device. Earlier acceptance gaps remain unchanged; production-wide financial-row-count invariance was not measured.

Documentation-only sync: the docs merge SHA is not the deployed runtime SHA and does not activate another release.
